data.name: Muzhaffar
data.gender_notes: Muzhaffar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Muzhaffar means steadfast and victorious in Arabic. It is derived from the root verb 'z-h-r', which means to remain steadfast or to support. This name is often given to a boy to inspire strength and perseverance. The name Muzhaffar carries the meaning “Steadfast, Victorious” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muzhaffar usually hope their child will grow to embody steadfast, victorious and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of faith and resilience
data.etymology: Muzhaffar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Steadfast, Victorious.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muzhaffar total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: مظفر
in_arabic.long_meaning: مظفر (Muthaffar) means strong, brave and victorious in Arabic. The name Muzaffar is derived from the Arabic root word 'Thafara' which means to be strong, to protect and to defend. The name is popular among Muslims due to its association with courage and strength.

in_urdu.name: مظفر
in_urdu.long_meaning: The Urdu translation of the name Muzhaffar is 'مظلوم سے محفوض' (Muzloom se Mahfooz), which means 'Protected from the Oppressed'. This name is believed to bestow strength and courage upon the child, and to shield them from harm.

in_hindi.name: मुठफ़फर
in_hindi.long_meaning: The Hindi translation of the name Muzhaffar is 'मुठफ़फर' (Mutthafar), which means 'strong, brave and bow-wielding'. The name is popular among Hindus as well as Muslims, and is believed to bestow strength, courage and protection upon the child.

in_pashto.name: مظفر
in_pashto.long_meaning: The Pashto translation of the name Muzhaffar is 'لوغوی، بلوار' (Logoi, Bolwar), which means 'strong, brave and warrior'. This name is popular among Pashtuns, and is believed to bestow strength, courage and martial prowess upon the child.

historical_references.reference: Muzaffar ibn Sebuktigin, the founder of the Ghaznavid Empire in 977 AD. He was a Turkish warrior who gained control over Ghazni and expanded his territory through military conquests, including the capture of Lahore in 1005 AD.

historical_references.reference: Muzaffar Shah III of Gujarat, who ruled from 1537 to 1554 AD. He was a powerful ruler who defeated the forces of the Mughal Emperor Humayun and briefly captured the throne of Delhi. His capital was Ahmedabad and he is known for his patronage of art and architecture.
historical_references.context: Mughal Empire, Delhi, Ahmedabad, Art and architecture

Overall, the name Muzhaffar represents a modern expression of Islamic identity and pride.
